title: Pointing at the Object: ezt / azt

sections.content: When 'this one' or 'that one' is the direct object -- with no noun named -- ez and az themselves take the accusative ending: ezt ('this one') and azt ('that one'). The pronoun alone carries the meaning.

items.english: I'd like this one, not that one.
Which one would you like? I'd like this one.

sections.content: ezt and azt are already complete accusative forms -- don't add a second -t. And don't confuse them with ez/az, which are used only when the thing is the subject, not the object.
